INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What should you do before acting on a spoken instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Move at once
   B. Listen to all of it
   C. Laugh
   D. Look away

2. Why should you underline new words in a text? (1 mark)
   A. To spoil the book
   B. So you can find their meanings and learn them
   C. To hide them
   D. To count pages

3. Vocabulary means (1 mark)
   A. the pictures in a book
   B. only names
   C. only long words
   D. all the words you know and can use

4. What is a good response when you did not understand an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Guess quietly
   B. Leave
   C. Politely ask the speaker to repeat it
   D. Do anything

5. What does an oral text mean? (1 mark)
   A. A text drawn on paper
   B. A text printed only
   C. A text written on a wall
   D. A text that is spoken

6. What should you do first when you give an instruction to a friend? (1 mark)
   A. Walk away
   B. Shout
   C. Plan the steps in order
   D. Say all steps at once quickly

7. What is reader's theatre? (1 mark)
   A. Reading a script aloud with different parts
   B. Acting with costumes only
   C. A drawing lesson
   D. A reading test

8. What is the first thing to do when someone gets a burn? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Put the burn under cool running water
   C. Cover it with dirt
   D. Rub it hard

9. What does listening for comprehension mean? (1 mark)
   A. Listening only to music
   B. Listening to understand and remember
   C. Listening while sleeping
   D. Listening without thinking

10. What should you do when a stranger offers you a lift? (1 mark)
   A. Go with them
   B. Accept sweets
   C. Give your name
   D. Say no politely and tell a trusted adult

11. What is the main idea of a paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. The last word
   B. The number of lines
   C. What the paragraph is mostly about
   D. The title font

12. What is the lesson of the hare and tortoise story? (1 mark)
   A. Hares are lazy
   B. Tortoises are fast
   C. Never race
   D. Slow and steady wins the race

13. What does Asiyesikia la mkuu huvunjika guu teach? (1 mark)
   A. Elders are always wrong
   B. Never walk
   C. Someone who ignores elders' advice may get hurt
   D. Legs are weak

14. How should you collect proverbs from an elder? (1 mark)
   A. Take it without asking
   B. Interrupt
   C. Greet politely and listen to the whole proverb
   D. Refuse to listen

15. What does a conjunction do? (1 mark)
   A. Describes a colour
   B. Shows a feeling
   C. Names a thing
   D. Joins words or sentences

16. Which interjection fits a small mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Hurray
   B. Wow
   C. Bravo
   D. Oops

17. What is a debate? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of poem
   B. A song
   C. A discussion in which two sides give opposite views with reasons
   D. A game of football

18. Which interjection shows surprise? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck
   B. Wow
   C. Shh
   D. Ouch

19. What is a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. A map
   B. A conversation between two or more people
   C. A long description
   D. A list

20. Where can you find correct interjections for your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. By inventing them
   B. By guessing
   C. By copying from another language
   D. By listening to and asking elders and teachers

21. What should you do after writing a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Never look at it
   B. Tear it
   C. Hide it
   D. Read it aloud with a partner

22. What should you do if you dialled a wrong number? (1 mark)
   A. Say sorry and end the call politely
   B. Call again angrily
   C. Stay silent
   D. Shout at them

23. Why do we match devices to their uses? (1 mark)
   A. To lose them
   B. To know what each is for
   C. To hide them
   D. To break them

24. What is a product? (1 mark)
   A. A thing made or grown for sale
   B. A poem
   C. A place
   D. A time

25. What should you do first before filling a form? (1 mark)
   A. Fold it
   B. Fill any box
   C. Read all the instructions
   D. Sign

26. What should you use to fill a form unless told otherwise? (1 mark)
   A. A pen
   B. A crayon
   C. A finger
   D. A chalk

27. What is a panel discussion? (1 mark)
   A. A solo song
   B. A quiz
   C. A planned discussion by a small group before an audience
   D. A game of football

28. What does answer when they call mean in the model poem? (1 mark)
   A. A leader shouts
   B. A leader hides
   C. A leader responds when people need them
   D. A leader sleeps

29. What is a poem's title? (1 mark)
   A. Its last line
   B. Its name
   C. Its rhyme
   D. Its page

30. Why should instruction charts use large clear letters? (1 mark)
   A. To use more ink
   B. So people can read them from a distance
   C. To make them heavy
   D. To hide meaning

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write an advert of four sentences for hand-made baskets. Include a headline, two adjectives, a price and where to buy. (5 marks)

32. Create a form with four fields to find out classmates' favourite games. Include a title and instructions. (4 marks)

33. Write a paragraph of four sentences about a time you handled money. Use when at least twice. (5 marks)

34. Add capital letters, commas and full stops: on friday we bought rice beans and flour (3 marks)

35. Give two rules for filling in a form correctly. (2 marks)

36. Complete with a simile: The baby slept like a ______. (2 marks)

37. Describe how a class can collect and keep cultural songs from the community. (4 marks)

38. Read: The nurse bandaged the wound gently and the blood stopped. What does wound mean? Give two clues. (3 marks)

39. Name two parts of an advert. (2 marks)

40. Name four question words used to check comprehension. (2 marks)

41. Rewrite correctly: we live in nairobi (2 marks)

42. Explain the difference between skimming and scanning. (2 marks)

43. Write the verbs in this instruction: Close the door and sit down. (2 marks)

44. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about why we should write neatly. Check your capital letters and full stops. (5 marks)

45. Explain how the meaning of You are coming to school changes when it is a statement and when it is a question. (3 marks)

46. Explain what a story setting is. (2 marks)

47. Name two prepositions used to show position. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Listen to all of it
   Listening to the end helps you act correctly.

2. B — So you can find their meanings and learn them
   Underlining marks the words to study.

3. D — all the words you know and can use
   Vocabulary is a person's collection of words.

4. C — Politely ask the speaker to repeat it
   Polite questions help you understand.

5. D — A text that is spoken
   Oral means spoken.

6. C — Plan the steps in order
   Planning helps to give clear instructions.

7. A — Reading a script aloud with different parts
   Pupils read parts with expression.

8. B — Put the burn under cool running water
   Cool water reduces pain and damage.

9. B — Listening to understand and remember
   Comprehension is understanding.

10. D — Say no politely and tell a trusted adult
   Personal safety means not going with strangers.

11. C — What the paragraph is mostly about
   The main idea is the central point.

12. D — Slow and steady wins the race
   The tortoise wins by steady effort.

13. C — Someone who ignores elders' advice may get hurt
   It means one who does not listen to the elders may come to harm.

14. C — Greet politely and listen to the whole proverb
   Politeness and careful listening are important.

15. D — Joins words or sentences
   Conjunctions are joining words.

16. D — Oops
   Oops shows a small mistake.

17. C — A discussion in which two sides give opposite views with reasons
   A debate is an organised argument of a motion.

18. B — Wow
   Wow is used for surprise.

19. B — A conversation between two or more people
   A dialogue is people talking.

20. D — By listening to and asking elders and teachers
   Speakers know the correct forms.

21. D — Read it aloud with a partner
   Reading aloud shows if it sounds natural.

22. A — Say sorry and end the call politely
   Politeness matters.

23. B — To know what each is for
   Knowing the use helps us choose the right device.

24. A — A thing made or grown for sale
   A product is a thing for sale.

25. C — Read all the instructions
   Reading first prevents mistakes.

26. A — A pen
   A pen gives clear permanent writing.

27. C — A planned discussion by a small group before an audience
   A panel discusses a topic.

28. C — A leader responds when people need them
   It means to respond to people's needs.

29. B — Its name
   The title names the poem.

30. B — So people can read them from a distance
   Clarity helps readers.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any advert with a headline, two adjectives, a price and a place, for example: Strong Baskets for Sale. Our baskets are big and colourful. Only 300 shillings each. Buy at the market gate.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the four required features and one mark for clear sentences.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Title: Favourite Games. Instructions: Write neatly. Fields: Name, Class, Favourite game, Date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for title, one for instructions, two for four fields.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two uses of when, for example When I reached the shop, I counted my money. When I paid, I received change. I was happy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear sentence and one mark for correct use of when.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: On Friday we bought rice, beans and flour.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capitals, one mark for the commas, one for the full stop.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Read instructions first, write neatly inside the spaces, give true information, sign and date it (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: log (or a stone, or any suitable comparison)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a suitable comparison and one for keeping like.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ask elders politely, listen carefully, write or record the song with permission, note the name of the person who shared it and the date, and store it in a class portfolio.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct steps.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wound is an injury. Clues are the nurse, bandaged and blood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and two marks for clues, awarding one for each up to two.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Headline, picture, description, price, contact details (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Who, what, where, when, why, how (any four).
   Working / marking points: One mark for two correct question words and two marks for four.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: We live in Nairobi.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capital letters and one for the full stop.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Skimming is quick reading for the main idea and scanning is quick searching for a specific fact.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: close, sit
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three neat, complete sentences, for example Neat writing helps others to read my work. It shows respect for the reader. I feel proud when my book is tidy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence, one mark for capital letters and one for full stops.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: As a statement the voice falls and it tells something. As a question the voice rises and it asks something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the two meanings and one mark for the voice movement.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: The setting is the place and time where the story happens.
   Working / marking points: One mark for place and one for time.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: on, in, under, behind, beside, between, in front of, outside (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
